title.narrative: Counties achieving a reduction in the prevalence of selected zoonotic diseases or other health threats as a result of project-supported activities

comment.narrative: The indicator currently states that counties must achieve a reduction in the prevalence of selected zoonotic diseases or other health threats. However, such a reduction may only be documented by extensive interventions beyond the project period. Improved epidemiological surveillance could actually increase recorded incidence and prevalence during project implementation, as more cases are likely to be detected as a result of the improved surveillance system. Restructuring: this indicator to be replaced with "Share of priority zoonotic diseases and other health threats events that meet the One Health 7-1-7 standard (percentage)".

title.narrative: Public communication campaigns to increase public awareness about the risk of human exposure to wildlife in project provinces or counties

comment.narrative: The indicator measures the number of distinct public communication campaigns carried out at national and/or province and/or sub-province level. These campaigns are defined as efforts to inform, persuade, or motivate behavior changes in the public about zoonotic disease risks stemming from wildlife, human exposure to wildlife, threats of illegal wildlife trade, emerging health threats and other related topics. Each campaign will need to identify a well-defined audience at the appropriate level, and organize communication activities involving different media for a defined period of time. The first campaign is expected to be launched in April 2026. Restructuring: this indicator will be modified to reflect the broader topics of public communication on One Health: "Public communication campaigns to increase public awareness about One Health, in particular the risk of human exposure to wildlife in project provinces or counties (Number)”

title.narrative: Wildlife epidemic disease monitoring stations strengthened by the project and accredited to national standards

comment.narrative: Through the project, a selected number of the most critical stations at the national, provincial and sub-provincial networks are being upgraded, and planned to be completed in 2026. These stations will be producing information needed for the risk assessments, hotspot analysis, and for the multi-agency platform monitoring zoonoses.

title.narrative: Wet markets piloting ‘healthy marketplaces practices supported by the project

comment.narrative: Wet markets (community agriculture markets) will adapt Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) approach for piloting ‘healthy marketplaces concept by (i) segregating dry areas from wet areas (seafood, poultry, meat products, etc.) in marketspaces for avoiding cross-contamination; (ii) making improvements in food hygiene, water and sanitation utilities; (iii) enforcing weekly closres for cleaning and disinfection of marketplaces; (iv) promoting good animal health and animal welfare practices; (v) deploying digital technologies for better animal disease and food safety surveillance; and (vi) undertaking systematic risk communication campaigns. The pilot is launched in both project province and planned to be completed by June 2027.

title.narrative: Center for Disease Control and Prevention, veterinary and food safety laboratories supported by the project networked and strengthened for accreditation to relevant national or international standards

comment.narrative: CDC, veterinary, food safety and other relevant laboratories need upgrades for better surveillance of animal diseases and food borne pathogens. This indicator measures those upgrades that manage to bring the laboratories to comply with national standards, or international standards as applicable. Actual value is low due to ongoing procurement and upgrades that are not completed and in place. Currently, the project is supporting the exchange of information between sectoral surveillance systems towards a functioning surveillance network. The laboratories under these surveillance systems are not directly networked. Restructuring: this indicator to be modified to: "Center for Disease Control and Prevention, veterinary, food safety and other relevant laboratories supported by the project strengthened for accreditation to relevant national or international standards."

title.narrative: Grievances registered and addressed related to the delivery of project benefits

comment.narrative: Measures the percentage of grievances which have been received and have appropriately been addressed. As of December 12, 2025, 39 procurement-related complaints have been received, all of which have been resolved.

title.narrative: Staff trained by the project in joint field epidemiological programs under a One Health approach

comment.narrative: This indicator keeps track of the number of Government staff trained on field epidemiological programs with a One Health approach, provided to health, animal and wildlife professionals. Restructuring, this indicator will be slighted modified to reflect the broader topics of One Health training under the project: "Staff trained by the project under a One Health approach (Number)”

title.narrative: Multi-Sectoral Plans prepared and implemented under the project and achieving their performance targets

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the number of Multi-Sectoral Plans (MSP) that are prepared and implemented under the project at provincial and/or sub-provincial level. MSP must demonstrate multi-sectoral actions in selected areas such as: (a) Joint field epidemiological training for effective disease surveillance and investigation; (b) Local collaboration of laboratory services; (c) Establishing cross sectoral information sharing; (d) Joint outbreak investigation and response plans and coordinating prevention and control strategies; (e) Developing preparedness and response plans, establishment of rapid response team (drills, tabletop simulation exercises), training of sectoral spokespersons on risk communication; (f) Implementation of zoning/compartmentalization strategies (biosecurity infrastructure, disease surveillance, prevention and control) for specified animal species: (g) Promoting ‘healthy marketplace’ practices in the local wet markets; and (h) Other One Health related topics.

title.narrative: Policies, guidelines, notices, and other relevant government strategy documents revised incorporating One Health approaches conforming to global and regional good practices

baseline.value: Existing policies, regulations, notices and other strategy documents related to human health, animal health and wildlife health do not sufficiently include a One Health approach in project provinces

target.value: At least 6 policies, guidelines, notices or other relevant government strategy documents have been revised and issued.

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the revisions that are made to policy frameworks. It applies to the revision of policies, guidelines, notices, or other relevant government strategy documents, which are improved to incorporate a One Health approach. They cover both sectoral instruments (carried out for one sector in particular) and also multi-sector instruments.

actual.value: 5 policies, regulations, notices and other strategy documents related to human health, animal health and wildlife health updated incorporating a One Health approach in project provinces.

title.narrative: Multi-sectoral monitoring of zoonoses and other emerging health threats is established, and is generating and communicating information for action in project-supported provinces

comment.narrative: Currently, limited exchange of information between human, animal and wildlife health is recorded. Through the project, a multi-sectoral system will be established, to facilitate exchange of information and combine information and data to take a comprehensive view for monitoring zoonoses and other emerging health threats. The system will be able to overlap and provide reports and information resulting in the combination of layers. Criteria will be developed in the operations manual to define what specifics the system needs to comply with for the indicator to be changed to Yes. Participating provinces might target zoonotic risks, or other health threats suh as AMR.

title.narrative: Guidelines reflecting One Health approaches for cross-border inspection and quarantine systems for animal and plant products in Hainan developed and implemented
Cross-sectoral management mechanism for One Health established in Hainan and meeting regularly

comment.narrative: Achieved in Hainan. Cross sectoral management mechanisms include at least one of the following functions: a) governance: b) administrative: c) supervision: d) regulatory. Restructuring: this indicator will be modified to include Jiangxi: "Cross-sectoral management mechanism for One Health established in project provinces and meeting regularly (Yes/No)"

title.narrative: Quality of surveillance system improved in selected project counties

baseline.value: Surveillance system in selected project counties has a divergence when compared to independent serological surveys. The specific divergence will be determined when the independent survey is carried out.

target.value: The divergence between the surveillance system and the independent serological surveys in selected project counties has reduced. The final target percentage will be determined after the first year of project implementation.

comment.narrative: The MTR identified that the methodology of data collection for this indictor through independent serological surveys was considered impractical due to significant challenges in securing representative sampling, logistical coordination, and regulatory restrictions on collection of biomedical data. Addressing these challenges can be complex and time-consuming, making it difficult to implement within the project's timelines and operational framework. Restructuring: the MTR proposed replacing the indicator with “Percentage of surveillance reports for priority infectious diseases and other health threats provided within a mandated timeframe”.

actual.value: Surveillance system in selected project counties has a divergence when compared to independent serological surveys. The specific divergence will be determined when the independent survey is carried out.
